articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex plunges over 600 points, NSE Nifty50 slips below 25,200
articles.full_text: BSE Sensex dropped 637.57 points, or 0.77%, to 81,894.62, while NSE Nifty50 declined 204.50 points, or 0.81%, to 25,182.90. The fall followed a strong run in November, with the Sensex gaining nearly 11% and the Nifty advancing more than 10% up to November 17. Tuesday's session had also ended on a positive note, marking the second consecutive day of gains for the benchmark indices. The Sensex closed 427.40 points higher at 82,532.19, registering a rise of 0.52%. The Nifty settled at 25,387.40, up 96.30 points or 0.38%. Meanwhile, Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was down 0.69% at $92.53 per barrel. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) remained net buyers of equities, purchasing shares worth Rs 4,195.38 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data. Among Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 were trading higher. However, Shanghai's SSE Composite and Hong Kong's Hang Seng were in negative territory. Benchmark indices continued to trade in red on Wednesday, with selling pressure across most sectors keeping the market in the red. BSE Sensex was down 473.32 points, or 0.57%, at 82,058.87, while Nifty50 slipped 159.40 points, or 0.63%, to 25,262.60. The weakness was not limited to the frontline indices. Fourteen of the 16 major sectors recorded losses, while the mid-cap segment declined 0.6%. Small-cap stocks, meanwhile, traded largely unchanged. Metal shares faced sharper selling, with the sectoral index dropping 1.6%. Lower global metal prices weighed on the segment as the US dollar strengthened amid rising expectations of further interest rate hikes in the US. The stronger dollar also makes metals more expensive for buyers dealing in other currencies, adding to the pressure on prices. Dalal Street has recorded substantial gains in November, with Nifty50 rising 10.1% and Sensex advancing 10.8% so far during the month. The rally has also been particularly sharp over a shorter period, with the Nifty gaining 13% in just 12 sessions. Against this backdrop, some consolidation in the market is warranted, according to Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president of research at Bajaj Broking. The benchmarks had closed at near nine-month highs in the previous session, setting the stage for expectations of a breather after the strong upward run. The possibility of consolidation is among the key factors shaping the near-term market outlook.

articles.title: CISCE SHINE 2026 records three million student responses, assessment window open until December 15
articles.description: CISCE has launched SHINE 2026, a mandatory digital diagnostic assessment for students of Classes 4, 6 and 9 in affiliated schools. Within 48 hours of its November 15 launch, nearly 450 schools had commenced testing, with more than three million student responses recorded. The assessment covers English, Mathematics, Science and socio-emotional competencies. Aligned with NCF-SE 2023, the initiative builds on a previous pilot involving one lakh students across 273 schools. Testing closes on December 15.
